prompt: Use the Browser app to perform a complete, evidence-based analysis of https://missclick.net/. The site is a JavaScript application: you must inspect it through the Browser tools and base the report only on states, pages, DOM content, network activity, console output, storage, links, forms, controls, and behavior you actually observe. Explore the site's reachable visible navigation and meaningful interactive states systematically. Inspect rendered DOM/HTML where useful, exercise relevant interactions, inspect console and network logs, and record the exact URLs and page/state transitions you visit. Report: site purpose and structure; all pages/routes and significant UI states actually discovered; navigation and interactive elements; forms/inputs and their behavior; client-side technologies or implementation details directly evidenced by the browser; cookies/local/session storage observed; notable network requests/responses and external services; console errors/warnings; security/privacy-relevant observations supported by evidence; accessibility/usability observations supported by the rendered interface; and a concise inventory of discovered links/resources. Clearly distinguish observed facts from anything not verified. Do not use prior knowledge or invent unvisited routes. Include enough concrete evidence (URLs, visible labels/headings, selectors or DOM snippets where useful, request URLs/statuses where useful) to make the analysis auditable.

Use the Code Workspace app to enumerate every file present in the entire workspace created from the vulnerable-webapp template. Traverse the workspace recursively and do not omit hidden files. Return a deterministic, lexicographically sorted list of workspace-relative file paths. Include files only, not directories. Verify the result using Code Workspace; do not guess from the template name or prior knowledge.
